title: matba: a single-file press for poster-derived books, from intake to DOI
description:
matba is a single-file, dependency-free application that automates the whole path from a folder of poster images to a published, sealed and DOI-minted book: intake with content-hash de-duplication, a plate table, a doctor that refuses to build on known-defective input, payload generation in the kitab schema, and a generated seeder that creates the forge repository, seals a manifest, pushes with a verified postcondition, enables Pages, OpenTimestamps-stamps its artefacts and mints through Zenodo.

It provides a local web interface, an equivalent command-line interface and a Colab notebook over one engine. It reimplements neither git, the forge client nor the DOI client; it drives them, and reads a tool's interface at run time rather than assuming a remembered signature.

The design responds to a concrete failure mode. Three books were published by three near-identical scripts derived from one another by textual substitution, each copy inheriting its predecessor's defects and contributing a new one, including template placeholder files that reached a permanent record. matba emits one parameterised seeder so the engine exists once, and every check in its doctor corresponds to a defect that previously reached a live DOI.

Irreversible operations are gated: publication and minting each require an exact typed word, a mismatch aborts without recording anything, and a rehearsal environment that is itself unavailable is reported as such rather than treated as a failed artefact.
